target_moa.text: Crofelemer is an inhibitor of both the cAMP-stimulated CFTR chloride ion channel and the calcium-activated chloride channels (CaCC) at the luminal membrane of enterocytes, which regulate chloride and fluid secretion by intestinal epithelial cells; it acts by blocking chloride secretion and accompanying water loss.

citations.quote: Crofelemer is an inhibitor of both the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)-stimulated cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) chloride ion (Cl^-) channel, and the calcium-activated Cl^- channels (CaCC) at the luminal membrane of enterocytes. The CFTR Cl^- channel and CaCC regulate Cl^- and fluid secretion by intestinal epithelial cells.
Crofelemer is thought to act by blocking chloride ion secretion and accompanying high volume water loss, thereby normalizing the flow of chloride and water in the gastrointestinal tract.
